note: The node-to-cluster enhancement was implemented and run four times. Each configuration is recorded with what it revealed; the last one is the report's basis.

attempts.outcome: the commitment term decided the model: its value was 0.55 against the ranking hinge's 0.0156, the ranking was never optimised (its loss stayed at its initial 0.0156), and the hard partition collapsed -- 87.4% of the items on one community, the separation back to zero.

the ranking signal was rescued (the separation rose) but the soft usage constraint could not see the hard partition: every model put 82% to 99.7% of its items on one community while its soft usage stayed uniform, and the AF3 gap and the transitivity inflated for that reason alone.

attempts.assignment: the baseline's balanced plan, five iterations
attempts.outcome: the node-to-cluster terms raised the separation hugely (+0.167 over the model without them, p = 0) and again folded 54.7% of the items into one community: on a near-decision cost five iterations leave the plan's columns unbalanced by tens of percent.

attempts.assignment: the baseline's balanced plan, one hundred iterations
attempts.outcome: the hard partition is balanced for every model (largest community 1.77% to 1.86%, 62.7 to 63.8 effective communities out of 64), so the hard metrics are trustworthy -- and the node-to-cluster terms improve the soft separation by 14% (p = 0) while leaving the AF3 gap and the cohesion slightly lower.
